pages: Bias and Variance Prediction errors can be decomposed into two main components: error from bias, and error from variance1 Bias occurs with an underfit model, which is too simple to accurately model the relationship between input features X and some target Y Variance arises from an overfit model that memorizes the training data points, making it unable to generalize on the unseen data The objective is to minimize the generalization (test) error by selecting the appropriate modeling approach to find the trade-off between overfitting and underfitting2 1. Unbiased estimators In statistics, bias is understood as accuracy and variance as precision of an estimate, and no trade- off can be made for unbiased estimators1 In particular, bias is the distance between the average of the collection of estimates and the true average value of the parameter being estimated For an unbiased estimator, the bias is equal to 0, hence the error is typically composed only of the variance component2 To the right, we show how with an increasing sample size, the score function (gradient) approaches the true Maximum Likelihood Estimate (MLE) 1.
